items.title: 'Fall 2' reaches new heights in VFX
items.excerpt: Koala FX breaks down its VFX for the survival-thriller sequel, including how it stress-tested Flawless's AI tools (TrueSync, first used to redub lines on 'Fall') and fed back VFX-pipeline know-how such as de-grain and flicker handling to the AI developers.
items.hit_term: Flawless TrueSync / AI dubbing lip sync

items.title: The Next Generation Speaks: What Young VFX Artists Are Doing Differently
items.excerpt: Gen Z VFX artists split on AI: some see artist-driven machine-learning tools reshaping workflows rather than replacing artists, others reject prompt-generated imagery as replacing the human touch in cinema.

items.title: This Voice-Controlled Camera App Can Record Portrait and Landscape Video For You at the Same Time
items.excerpt: Shootsolo, a voice-controlled camera app and AI filming assistant for solo filmmakers and creators, adds simultaneous portrait and landscape recording to its feature set.

items.title: Ava DuVernay Didn't Make a Sequel — She Made '14th'
items.excerpt: DuVernay explains that degraded archival photos from boxes, slides and family albums couldn't reach film resolution, so she worked with Natasha Lyonne's Asteria Film Co., whose AI-powered tools restored them. (ComingSoon/World of Reel report a backlash over the film's AI-animated archival images.)
items.hit_term: Asteria / AI documentary ethics / AI restoration

items.title: Union releases guidelines to protect voice actors from AI
items.excerpt: The Japan Actors Union issued its first AI guidelines on Oct. 15, requiring consent before voices are used to train generative AI or to make AI audio replicating them, and broadly barring AI use of deceased actors' voices or AI as a replacement in foreign-language dubbing.
items.hit_term: Equity/union AI provisions, AI dubbing (off-list: no allowed outlet covered it)

items.title: As Hollywood fights AI, a new filmmaking hub takes shape in Culver City
items.excerpt: AI film studios such as Promise are clustering in Culver City and recruiting emerging and out-of-work creatives to reinvent traditional filmmaking. 'It's a great breeding ground for this new filmmaking,' says Promise co-founder Dave Clark.

items.title: Innovation vs job losses in local AI film 'Mountain of Graves'
items.excerpt: South Africa's Dragon Studios made 'Mountain of Graves' on AI filmmaking platforms and was selected for the Neu Wave AI Film Festival at LA Tech Week. Director Donovan Marsh says an AI film isn't one-click: it closely mirrors traditional filmmaking, with software replacing physical sets.

items.title: 'Niu Lai': Chinese Animation's Crude Contender
items.excerpt: Why global audiences embraced the amateur-made Chinese animated feature 'Niu Lai': its human-made flaws read as a counterpoint to the 'soulless factory line of generative AI' encroaching on animation.

items.title: Generate Crew seeks generative VFX trainee for 'high-profile' production in Sydney
items.excerpt: Generate Crew is recruiting a generative VFX trainee for an unannounced, high-profile streaming production shooting in Sydney, an early sign of 'generative VFX' becoming a dedicated crew role.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly wants to bring back Sora AI, but not everyone may be able to use it
items.excerpt: Per The Information, OpenAI is negotiating to license its shelved Sora video model to a stealth startup co-founded by Jeffrey Katzenberg and former Sora lead Bill Peebles, which would sell film-industry tools built on it. The deal is not final.
items.hit_term: Sora / studio AI licensing deal (off-list; deal unconfirmed)

items.title: Why Bot VFX chose artists over AI when the clock was ticking
items.excerpt: Bot VFX explains why it relied on artists rather than AI for a tight-deadline job, calling AI 'an accelerator, not a replacement' that 'works on probability' as machine learning reshapes VFX workflows.
